title: Randomness and Determinism
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of randomness and determinism in a PyTorch workflow.
Apply a small example of randomness and determinism and interpret the output.
Identify a relevant limitation, debugging check, or reproducibility concern.

content.intro: Randomness and Determinism: A model state_dict stores learnable parameters and persistent buffers. A training checkpoint may also need optimizer/scheduler state, epoch, metrics, and random states. In this lesson, use a small example to make the inputs, outputs, and boundary conditions explicit.
content.why_it_matters: Saving only weights is often enough for inference, but resuming training reproducibly requires restoring the state that affects subsequent updates. For this lesson, focus on random seeds and the evidence you can collect from a controlled example.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: Save only the data needed for the intended workflow, validate a restored model on a fixed input, and treat serialized files as trusted inputs only. The source topics for this lesson are: Random seeds, Python, NumPy, and PyTorch randomness, DataLoader worker seeding. Keep each topic connected to a checkable input/output behavior.

content_blocks.title: Read the example
content_blocks.text: Serialize a state dictionary, load it into the same architecture, and compare outputs with a fixed input to confirm the round trip. The example is a teaching-scale check, not evidence of a trained model score or a hardware-independent performance claim.

content_blocks.title: Guided PyTorch example
content_blocks.code:
import random, torch
random.seed(5); torch.manual_seed(5)
print(torch.rand(2).tolist())

content.task: Try it yourself: Save and restore a state_dict for a small model, assert outputs match, then list the extra metadata needed for resumable training. Record the observed result and one limitation; do not report an unrun training or performance result as measured.
task_acceptance_criteria: The experiment demonstrates at least one relevant aspect of randomness and determinism.
Record the expected and observed result, including shape/dtype/device information when relevant.
Explain one common failure mode, compatibility limitation, or evaluation caveat.
hints: Begin with the smallest working example for randomness and determinism and keep input shapes explicit.

troubleshooting.symptom: A tensor operation raises a shape, dtype, or device mismatch.
troubleshooting.check: Print .shape, .dtype, and .device for each input. Resolve the mismatch intentionally instead of changing dimensions blindly.

troubleshooting.symptom: The example fails because an optional package or accelerator is unavailable.
troubleshooting.check: Check the installed PyTorch/package versions and device availability. Use the official installation selector and run the CPU-compatible path where appropriate.

troubleshooting.symptom: The result differs across runs or machines.
troubleshooting.check: Fix the seed where useful, record versions and inputs, and document operations that remain nondeterministic or hardware dependent.

common_mistakes.problem: Relying on assumptions instead of inspecting the data or output.
common_mistakes.why: Many ML failures come from incorrect shapes, labels, preprocessing, or execution mode rather than a syntax error.
common_mistakes.fix: Inspect representative inputs and add assertions for the expected shape, dtype, range, or behavior.

common_mistakes.problem: Mixing training-time behavior with inference-time behavior.
common_mistakes.why: Dropout, normalization, gradient tracking, and optimizer updates can change how a model behaves.
common_mistakes.fix: Never load untrusted pickle-based checkpoint files; standard serialization can have security implications and compatibility limits.

common_mistakes.problem: Using a current or experimental API without recording its version assumptions.
common_mistakes.why: Hardware support and ecosystem APIs can change independently of the core package.
common_mistakes.fix: Pin compatible dependencies, record the environment, and test after upgrades.
